findings.summary: The chunking example caps the body text at 400 tokens and then prepends the title, so chunks can exceed the stated 400-token cap.
findings.evidence: "for part in cap_tokens(sec.text, 400):" ... "\"text\": sec.title + \"\\n\" + part" with the note "400-token cap per chunk"
findings.fix: Cap the body at 400 minus the title's token count, for example cap_tokens(sec.text, 400 - tokens(sec.title)). Alternatively, say that the cap applies to the body and the title is extra.

findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "reciprocal", "combines").
findings.evidence: Hybrid search combines dense vectors (meaning) with BM25 keywords (exact IDs, names, error codes). Merge the two ranked lists with Reciprocal Rank Fusion: score = Σ 1/(60 + rank).
findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.

findings.summary: HyDE and query rewriting are named but never explained, so a learner cannot tell what either does or why it helps.
findings.evidence: "Query rewriting and HyDE help vague or multi-turn questions"
findings.fix: Add one line for each. Query rewriting: an LLM turns the question into a standalone search query. HyDE: the LLM writes a hypothetical answer, and that text is embedded for retrieval instead of the question.

findings.summary: Page 4 and page 6 give different retrieval depths for the same step.
findings.evidence: Page 4: "fetch top-k chunks (k often 5-20)" and the rerank diagram "Top 50"; page 6: "Retrieve top 20-50, rerank to 5"
findings.fix: Use one range everywhere. For example, on page 4 write "fetch top 20-50 candidates" for the reranker input, and keep "k = 5-20" only for the case with no reranker.

findings.summary: A single bullet holds two separate ideas, what dense search is for and what BM25 is for.
findings.evidence: "Dense = meaning; BM25 = IDs, names, error codes"
findings.fix: Split it into two bullets, one for dense and one for BM25. Or add a small two-row table of Dense vs BM25 with columns for strength and misses.

findings.summary: Two adjacent bullets give conflicting chunk ordering rules.
findings.evidence: "Dedupe near-identical chunks; order by relevance" followed by "Best chunks first and last; middle recalled worst"
findings.fix: Merge them into one rule: "Order by relevance, then place the best chunks at the start and end of the context". Split the dedupe step into its own bullet.
